nodes.title: Learn reinforcement learning by writing the learning algorithms yourself, one piece at a time.
Every trained agent is measured against a random player and a simple scripted bot, so "it learned" means something.
Every result can be explained, with the saved evidence from each run to back it up.
Any trained agent can be watched playing, as a replay.
A shared core (environment interface, training loop, logging, replay viewer) makes each new environment cheaper than the last.
The game is played on a fixed 10×10 board of open cells surrounded by walls.

criteria: Given any game, when it starts, then the board has 10×10 open cells, walls on all four sides, a snake of length 3 in the middle row heading right, and exactly one food on an empty cell.
Given any training run or test game, when the board size is read, then it is 10×10.

nodes.title: On each move the agent chooses one of 3 moves relative to its heading: straight, turn left, turn right.

criteria: Given a snake heading right, when it turns left, then its head moves up one cell and its heading becomes up.
Given any heading, when any of the 3 moves is chosen, then the snake never reverses into its own neck.

nodes.title: Eating food makes the snake 1 cell longer, gives a reward of +1, and places a new food on an empty cell.

criteria: Given food directly ahead, when the snake moves straight, then its length goes up by 1, the move's plain reward is +1, and one new food appears on a cell not covered by the snake.

nodes.title: Moving into a wall or into the snake's own body ends the game with a reward of −1.

criteria: Given the head next to a wall, when the snake moves into the wall, then the game ends and the move's reward is −1.
Given the head next to a body cell that will still be occupied after the move, when the snake moves into it, then the game ends and the move's reward is −1.

nodes.title: Every move that neither eats nor kills has a plain reward of 0.

criteria: Given a move into an empty cell, when it is made, then its plain reward is 0.

nodes.title: At every move the agent sees exactly 11 yes/no facts: danger straight, danger left, danger right; heading up, down, left, right; food is up, down, left, right of the head.

criteria: Given the head next to the top wall while heading up, when the facts are read, then "danger straight" is yes and "heading up" is yes.
Given food above and to the left of the head, when the facts are read, then "food is up" and "food is left" are yes and "food is down" and "food is right" are no.
Given a cell occupied by the body or a wall next to the head on its left, when the facts are read, then "danger left" is yes.

nodes.title: A game ends after 100 moves in a row without eating.

criteria: Given a snake that has gone 100 moves since its last food (or since the start), when the 100th move is made without eating, then the game ends and that move's plain reward is 0.

nodes.title: The same game seed and the same moves always give the same game.

criteria: Given a game seed and a list of moves, when the game is played twice, then every board, food position, reward and ending is identical.

nodes.title: The random player picks each move uniformly at random from the 3 moves.

criteria: Given 30,000 random-player moves, when the share of each move is counted, then each is between 32% and 35%.

nodes.title: The scripted bot moves toward the food, never making a move that kills it immediately when a safe move exists.

criteria: Given food to the left and the left cell free, when the bot moves, then it turns left.
Given food straight ahead and a wall straight ahead with the right cell free, when the bot moves, then it turns right.
Given several safe moves equally close to the food, when the bot moves, then it prefers straight, then left, then right.

nodes.title: When every move kills it, the scripted bot goes straight.

criteria: Given danger straight, left and right, when the bot moves, then it goes straight and the game ends.

nodes.title: The tank's random swimmer picks each move with a uniformly random direction and a speed drawn uniformly from 0 to 2.5 units per second.

criteria: Given 10,000 random-swimmer moves, when their directions are sorted into four equal quarters of the circle, then each quarter holds between 23% and 27% of them.
Given 10,000 random-swimmer moves, when their speeds are averaged, then the mean is between 1.2 and 1.3.

nodes.title: When the tank's scripted bot sees the ball, it swims at 2.5 units per second directly away from the ball.

criteria: Given the ball seen at relative position (1, 0), when the bot moves, then its swim velocity is (−2.5, 0).

nodes.title: When the tank's scripted bot doesn't see the ball, it stays still.

criteria: Given the ball seen as no, when the bot moves, then its swim velocity is (0, 0).

nodes.title: In each comparison, the tank baselines play with the same fish count and view radius as the learner they are compared with.

criteria: Given a 5-fish, wide-view learner, when its baselines are scored, then they play the same test tanks with 5 fish and the wide view.

nodes.title: The table learner updates the score of the move it just made from the reward plus the discounted best score of the situation it reached (a one-step Q-learning update), after every move.

criteria: Given a known table, situation, move, reward and next situation, when one update is applied, then the new score equals the hand-computed Q-learning update for the run's learning rate and discount.
Given a move that ended the game, when the update is applied, then the next situation contributes nothing.

nodes.title: While training, the table learner sometimes picks a random move instead of its best one, at a rate that falls over the run from a starting rate to a floor saved with the run's settings.

criteria: Given a run's exploration settings, when the rate is read at the start, the middle and the end of training, then it matches the saved schedule at each point.

nodes.title: During test games the table learner always picks its highest-scored move.

criteria: Given a trained table, when a test game is played twice from the same seed, then both games are identical.

nodes.title: The learning update is written in the project; no ready-made learning algorithm is used.

criteria: Given the trained table learner, when its learning steps are traced, then each one is code written in the project.

nodes.title: The plain rung learns from each move right after it is made, using that move's reward plus the discounted best score of the next situation as its target.

criteria: Given a known function, move, reward and next situation, when one update is applied, then the target equals the hand-computed value and the function's score for that move moves toward it.

nodes.title: The replay-buffer rung stores past moves and learns from batches drawn at random from that store.

criteria: Given a store of past moves and a seed, when a batch is drawn, then every move in it comes from the store and the same seed draws the same batch.
Given a store at its saved capacity, when a new move is added, then the oldest move is dropped.

nodes.title: The target-network rung computes its targets from a frozen copy of the learner, refreshed every fixed number of updates saved with the run's settings.

criteria: Given the refresh interval, when updates run between two refreshes, then the copy does not change; when the interval is reached, the copy equals the learner.

nodes.title: The Double DQN rung chooses the next situation's best move with the learner, and scores that move with the frozen copy.

criteria: Given a learner and a copy that disagree on the next situation's best move, when the target is computed, then it uses the copy's score for the learner's chosen move.

nodes.title: Each rung differs from the rung before only by the piece it adds; every other setting is the same.

criteria: Given the saved settings of two neighbouring rungs, when they are compared, then the only differences are the added piece and its own settings.

nodes.title: While training, each rung explores with the same falling random-move rate as TAB-02; during test games it always picks its highest-scored move.

criteria: Given a trained rung, when a test game is played twice from the same seed, then both games are identical.

nodes.title: The learning updates of every rung are written in the project; no ready-made learning algorithm is used.

criteria: Given any trained rung, when its learning steps are traced, then each one is code written in the project.

nodes.title: The shaped reward is the plain reward plus 0.1 for a move that brings the head closer to the food and minus 0.1 for a move that takes it further away, measured in grid steps to the food that was on the board before the move.

criteria: Given a move that cuts the distance to the food from 5 to 4, when it is made, then the shaped reward is +0.1.
Given a move that raises the distance from 4 to 5, when it is made, then the shaped reward is −0.1.
Given a move that eats the food, when it is made, then the shaped reward is +1.1.

nodes.title: A move that ends the game by collision has a shaped reward of −1, with no nudge.

criteria: Given a move into a wall, when it is made, then the shaped reward is −1.

nodes.title: Every Snake run uses either the plain or the shaped reward for training, and saves which.

criteria: Given a finished Snake run, when its saved settings are read, then they name its reward.

nodes.title: Test scores never use the shaped reward; they always count food eaten.

criteria: Given the same agent tested once after plain training and once after shaped training, when the scores are read, then both are food eaten per game.

nodes.title: The plain-versus-shaped comparison trains the Double DQN rung on each reward, with every other setting the same.

criteria: Given the plain and shaped runs of that comparison, when their saved settings are compared, then the only difference is the reward.

nodes.title: A training run trains one learner from one training seed on one environment setup: Snake with one reward (the table learner or one DQN rung), or the tank with one fish count and one view radius (one policy-gradient rung).

criteria: Given a learner, an environment setup and a seed, when a run is started with one action, then it trains that learner on that setup with that seed and nothing else.

nodes.title: Each run saves its settings, seed, learning curve, final agent and test games.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its saved evidence is opened, then all five are there.

nodes.title: Rerunning from a run's saved settings and seed gives the same result.

criteria: Given a finished run, when it is run again on the same laptop from its saved settings and seed, then the test score at every curve point is identical.

nodes.title: While a run trains, it shows the steps trained so far, the latest test score and the time elapsed.

criteria: Given a run in progress, when a curve point is reached, then the display updates all three.

nodes.title: A run never overwrites another run's evidence.

criteria: Given two runs with the same learner, reward and seed, when both finish, then both sets of evidence are kept.

nodes.title: A run that stops before it finishes is marked incomplete and is left out of every comparison.

criteria: Given a run stopped by hand partway through, when comparisons are made, then it is listed as incomplete and its numbers are not used.

nodes.title: A run still training at 60 minutes stops, saves what it has, and is marked over the time limit.

criteria: Given a run that reaches 60 minutes, when the limit passes, then training stops, its evidence so far is saved, it is marked over the time limit, and it is left out of every comparison.

nodes.title: Training, testing, saving evidence and replay work for a second environment without changes to them.

criteria: Given a minimal second environment used only for this check, when it is trained, tested and replayed, then none of the training, testing, saving or replay behavior had to change.

nodes.title: After the fish tank is added, Snake runs saved before it still reproduce, compare and replay identically.

criteria: Given a Snake run saved before the tank was added, when it is rerun on the same laptop from its saved settings and seed, then the test score at every curve point is identical to the saved one.
Given the Snake comparisons and replays made before the tank was added, when they are made again, then every result and every replayed game is identical.

nodes.title: Every agent is scored on the same 100 test games of its environment setup, each started from a fixed test seed that is never used in training.

criteria: Given any two agents on the same environment setup, when they are tested, then they play games from the same 100 test seeds.
Given any training run, when its game seeds are compared with the test seeds, then none match.

nodes.title: An agent's test score is the mean of its game scores over the 100 test games: food eaten per game in Snake, and the game score of TANK-10 (mean seconds survived per fish) in the tank.

criteria: Given 100 Snake test games with known food eaten, when the score is computed, then it equals their mean.
Given 100 tank test games with known game scores, when the score is computed, then it equals their mean.

nodes.title: Each run's learning curve is its test score against steps trained, at 20 evenly spaced points, with the random player's and the scripted bot's scores drawn as lines on the same chart; the chart follows the dataviz skill.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its curve is opened, then it shows 20 test scores in order of steps trained, plus both baseline lines.
Given the 5 seeds of one learner, when their combined curve is opened, then it shows the mean across seeds at each point with the spread across seeds.

nodes.title: Each learner's final agent is compared with each baseline using the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given the 100 test-game scores of each of the learner's 5 seed runs, and the baseline's scores on the same 100 games. The learner beats the baseline when its score is higher and the difference is significant at 5% after correcting for the number of comparisons in the report; it ties when the difference is not significant; otherwise it loses.

criteria: Given 5 complete seed runs of a learner, when the comparison is made, then the report states beats, ties or loses against each baseline, with the test's result.
Given fewer than 5 complete seed runs, when the comparison is requested, then it is not made, and the report lists the missing seeds.

nodes.title: Each added piece gets a before-and-after comparison with the rung below it, made the same way as EVAL-04. In Snake: table learner → plain DQN, plain → + replay buffer, + replay buffer → + target network, + target network → + Double DQN, and plain reward → shaped reward. In the tank: REINFORCE → + learned baseline, + learned baseline → actor-critic, actor-critic → PPO (all with 1 fish and the short view), 1-fish PPO → 5-fish PPO (short view), and 5-fish PPO short view → wide view. Every outcome counts: better, worse, or no difference.

criteria: Given 5 complete seed runs of both rungs, when the comparison is made, then the report states better, worse or no difference, with the test's result and both rungs' combined curves on one chart.

nodes.title: Every comparison result holds a written explanation; a result with no explanation is shown as unexplained.

criteria: Given a comparison result with an empty explanation, when the report is opened, then that result is marked unexplained.
Given a tie or a no-difference result with an explanation, when the report is opened, then it is marked explained.

nodes.title: Each environment is done when its top learner beats the random player, beats or ties the scripted bot, every comparison in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05 for that environment has a result, and every tie and no-difference result is explained. Snake's top learner is the Double DQN agent; the tank's is 5-fish, short-view PPO.

criteria: Given a Double DQN agent that beats both baselines and all comparisons made and explained, when the done check runs, then it reports done.
Given a Double DQN agent that ties the scripted bot with the tie explained, when the done check runs, then it reports done.
Given a tie with the scripted bot left unexplained, when the done check runs, then it reports not done and names the missing explanation.
Given a Double DQN agent that ties or loses to the random player, when the done check runs, then it reports not done.

Given 5-fish, short-view PPO that beats the random swimmer, ties the scripted bot with the tie explained, and every tank comparison made and explained, when the done check runs, then it reports the tank done.
Given 5-fish, wide-view PPO that beats the scripted bot while 5-fish, short-view PPO loses to it, when the done check runs, then it reports the tank not done.

nodes.title: Any saved test game of any saved agent, the baselines included, can be watched as a replay.

criteria: Given a finished run, when one of its test games is chosen, then the replay plays it from the first move to the end.

nodes.title: A Snake replay shows the board, the snake, the food, the move number, the food eaten so far, and how the game ended.

criteria: Given a replay at any move, when it is shown, then all of these are visible; at the end, the ending (wall, body, 100 moves without food, full board) is shown.

nodes.title: At every move of a Snake learner's game, the replay shows the agent's score for each of the 3 moves, with the chosen move marked.

criteria: Given a table learner or DQN replay at any move, when it is shown, then 3 scores are visible and the chosen one is marked.
Given a baseline replay, when it is shown, then the move scores are shown as not applicable.

nodes.title: The replay can be paused, resumed, and stepped forward one step at a time.

criteria: Given a paused replay, when "step" is chosen, then it advances exactly one step and stays paused.

nodes.title: The replay speed can be set from 1 to 30 steps per second.

criteria: Given a speed of 5 steps per second, when it plays for 10 seconds, then it advances 50 steps (±2).

nodes.title: A replay of a saved test game is identical to the game that was scored.

criteria: Given a saved test game, when it is replayed, then every state, move and score matches the saved game.

nodes.title: A saved agent can play and be watched on a fresh game from any seed chosen at the time.

criteria: Given a saved agent and a new seed, when the game is watched twice, then both games are identical.

nodes.title: A tank replay shows the tank, the ball, every fish still swimming, the time in seconds, the number of fish still swimming, and the time each removed fish was removed.

criteria: Given a tank replay at any step, when it is shown, then all of these are visible; at the end, the ending (every fish removed, or the 60-second cap) is shown.

nodes.title: At every step of a tank learner's game, each fish still swimming shows an arrow for its chosen swim velocity and a number for how sure it was: the spread of its move choice, smaller meaning surer.

criteria: Given a policy-gradient replay at any step, when it is shown, then every fish still swimming has an arrow and a spread number.
Given a tank baseline replay, when it is shown, then the arrows and spreads are shown as not applicable.

nodes.title: The tank is a circle of radius 10 holding one ball and a fixed number of fish, 1 or 5, saved with the run.

criteria: Given any tank game, when it starts, then the tank's radius is 10, it holds exactly one ball, and the number of fish is the run's 1 or 5.

nodes.title: The ball, of radius 0.5, moves at a constant 2 units per second and bounces off the tank wall like a mirror.

criteria: Given the ball reaching the wall, when it bounces, then it leaves at the same angle to the wall's normal as it arrived, on the other side of the normal.
Given any step of any game, when the ball's speed is measured, then it is 2 units per second.

nodes.title: Each game starts with the ball at the centre heading in a direction set by the game seed, and each fish at a seed-chosen spot between 5 units from the centre and the wall.

criteria: Given any game, when it starts, then the ball is at the centre and every fish is between 5 and 9.75 units from the centre.
Given the same game seed twice, when both games start, then the ball's direction and every fish's spot are identical.

nodes.title: Every 0.1 seconds of tank time, each fish still swimming chooses a move: a swim velocity (x, y) in tank directions, capped at a speed of 2.5 units per second.

criteria: Given a fish that chooses velocity (1, 0), when the step runs, then it moves 0.1 units in the x direction.
Given a fish that chooses velocity (3, 4), when the step runs, then it swims at 2.5 units per second in direction (0.6, 0.8) and moves 0.25 units.

nodes.title: A fish, of radius 0.25, can't leave the tank: a move that would carry it past the wall stops it at the wall.

criteria: Given a fish touching the wall that swims straight outward, when the step runs, then it stays inside the tank, touching the wall.

nodes.title: Fish swim through each other unharmed.

criteria: Given two fish whose paths cross, when the step runs, then both finish their moves and both are still swimming.

nodes.title: At the end of each step, the ball removes every fish whose edge touches it (centres within 0.75 units); a removed fish takes no more moves and is no longer seen by other fish.

criteria: Given a fish whose centre ends a step 0.7 units from the ball's centre, when the step ends, then the fish is removed.
Given a fish whose centre ends a step 0.8 units from the ball's centre, when the step ends, then the fish is still swimming.
Given a removed fish, when the other fish's views are read, then none of them sees it.

nodes.title: A tank game ends when every fish is removed, or at 60 seconds of tank time (600 steps); until then it goes on for the fish still swimming.

criteria: Given 5 fish of which 4 are removed, when the steps continue, then the game goes on until the last fish is removed or 600 steps have run.
Given a fish still swimming after 600 steps, when the 600th step ends, then the game ends.

nodes.title: A fish's reward is +0.1 for each step it survives, and 0 for the step in which it is removed, which ends its experience; there is no other reward.

criteria: Given a fish that survives a step, when the step ends, then its reward is +0.1.
Given a fish removed during a step, when the step ends, then its reward is 0 and it has no further steps.
Given a fish that survives all 600 steps, when its rewards are summed, then the total is 60.

nodes.title: A fish's score is the seconds of tank time it survived, from 0 to 60, and a game's score is the mean over all its fish, removed ones included.

criteria: Given 5 fish that survive 10, 20, 30, 60 and 60 seconds, when the game is scored, then its score is 36.
Given 1 fish removed at 12.5 seconds, when the game is scored, then its score is 12.5.

nodes.title: At every step, each fish sees exactly 11 numbers about what lies within its view radius: for the ball, whether it is seen, its position relative to the fish (2 numbers) and its velocity relative to the fish (2); for the wall, whether it is seen and the offset from the fish to the wall's nearest point (2); for the nearest other fish, whether it is seen and its position relative to the fish (2). Anything beyond the radius is seen as no, and its numbers are 0.

criteria: Given the short view and the ball 3 units away, when the fish's view is read, then the ball is seen as yes and its relative position and velocity are the true ones.
Given the short view and the ball 5 units away, when the view is read, then the ball is seen as no and its 4 numbers are 0.
Given the short view and a fish at the centre of the tank, when the view is read, then the wall is seen as no and its 2 numbers are 0.
Given a 1-fish game, when the view is read, then the nearest other fish is seen as no and its 2 numbers are 0.

nodes.title: A fish's view radius is either 4 units (the short view) or 20 units (the wide view, which spans the whole tank), saved with the run.

criteria: Given the wide view, when any fish's view is read at any step, then the ball and the wall are seen as yes, and so is the nearest other fish if one is still swimming.

nodes.title: The same game seed and the same moves always give the same game.

criteria: Given a game seed and a list of moves for every fish, when the game is played twice, then every position, removal, reward and ending is identical.

nodes.title: The REINFORCE rung, after each game, raises the chance of each move a fish made in proportion to the discounted return that followed it.

criteria: Given a known policy, a finished game, the run's learning rate and discount, when one update is applied, then the change to the policy equals the hand-computed REINFORCE step.

nodes.title: The learned-baseline rung weights each move by its return minus a learned estimate of the return from the situation it was made in, and trains that estimate toward the returns seen.

criteria: Given a move with return 4.0 from a situation estimated at 3.0, when its weight is computed, then the weight is 1.0.
Given a situation whose estimate is below the returns seen from it, when the estimate is trained, then the estimate rises toward them.

nodes.title: The actor-critic rung weights each move by its reward plus the discounted estimate of the next situation, minus the estimate of the situation it was made in, and learns after every fixed number of steps saved with the run's settings.

criteria: Given a known reward, discount and two estimates, when a move's weight is computed, then it equals the hand-computed value.
Given the run's steps per update, when training runs, then an update happens after every that many steps, not only at the end of a game.

nodes.title: The PPO rung learns from each batch of experience in a fixed number of passes, and caps each move's change in chance at a clip range, both saved with the run's settings.

criteria: Given a move whose chance has already risen past 1 + the clip range times its chance when collected, and a positive weight, when the update is computed, then that move pushes the policy no further.
Given the run's passes per batch, when one batch is learned from, then the number of passes equals it.

nodes.title: Each tank setup differs from the one it is compared with only by the piece it adds: one rung from the rung below, 5-fish PPO from 1-fish PPO only by the fish count, and wide-view PPO from short-view PPO only by the view radius.

criteria: Given the saved settings of any two setups compared in EVAL-05, when they are compared, then the only differences are the added piece and its own settings.

nodes.title: With several fish, every fish uses the same policy on its own view, and every fish's experience trains it.

criteria: Given a 5-fish run, when moves are chosen, then every fish's move comes from the one policy applied to that fish's own 11 numbers.
Given a 5-fish run, when an update is applied, then it learns from the experience of all 5 fish up to each one's removal.

nodes.title: While training, each fish picks its move at random from the policy's spread; during test games it takes the policy's most likely move.

criteria: Given a trained policy, when a test game is played twice from the same seed, then both games are identical.

nodes.title: The learning updates of every rung are written in the project; no ready-made learning algorithm is used.

criteria: Given any trained rung, when its learning steps are traced, then each one is code written in the project.

nodes.title: All training and test experience comes from the agents playing in the lab's environments, Snake and the fish tank; no outside data is used.

criteria: Given any run, when its inputs are listed, then the only source of games is the run's own environment, started from the run's own seeds.

nodes.title: Each training run in either environment, including its test games, finishes in under 1 hour (60 minutes) on the laptop's processor.

criteria: Checked by the elapsed time saved with each run; RUN-07 stops any run that reaches 60 minutes.

nodes.title: Training, testing and replay run on the Apple Silicon laptop with no NVIDIA graphics card.

criteria: Checked by running every learner's training, a comparison and a replay on that laptop.

`cli.main` merges overrides into `default_params`, prints one progress line per curve point, exits 2 with the choices on `UnknownName`; TC-11 passes
PL-01's pre-build sections replaced by a `dt layout` pointer

TC-07 passes for `dqn-double`; the learner picks `a*` and the frozen copy scores it; its hand-computed target sample matches; the lower rungs are unchanged
Given a clock past `max_minutes`, when `train_loop` reaches its next check, then it finishes `over_time` with the curve points so far saved
Given a `progress` callback raising `KeyboardInterrupt`, when it fires, then the run finishes `incomplete`

nodes.title: Snake rules hold on every move of random play
A game ends starved after 100 moves without food
Shaped reward nudges ±0.1 and never changes the score
Same seed and moves give the same game
Scripted bot never takes a fatal move when a safe one exists
Random player draws the 3 moves evenly
Every learner recovers a two-step chain's Bellman values
Test scores count food on the reserved seeds, greedily
Stopped runs are marked and never overwritten
A clearly better learner beats, a clearly worse one loses
A ladder pair differing beyond its added piece waits
Done only when Double DQN wins and every tie is explained
Every saved game replays as it was scored
A tampered saved game is refused at the first wrong move
A fresh seed plays the same game every time
Replay speed stays within 1–30 and pause/step count moves
Double DQN beats random and beats or ties the scripted bot
Score an agent on the test games
Find a run and watch one of its games

edges.reason: thickens the same module, on top of the replay rung (AD-03)
thickens the same module, on top of the target rung (AD-03)

nodes.title: Learn reinforcement learning by writing the learning algorithms yourself, one piece at a time.
Every trained agent is measured against a random player and a simple scripted bot, so "it learned" means something.
Every result can be explained, with the saved evidence from each run to back it up.
Any trained agent can be watched playing, as a replay.
A shared core (environment interface, training loop, logging, replay viewer) makes each new environment cheaper than the last.
The game is played on a fixed 10×10 board of open cells surrounded by walls.

criteria: Given any game, when it starts, then the board has 10×10 open cells, walls on all four sides, a snake of length 3 in the middle row heading right, and exactly one food on an empty cell.
Given any training run or test game, when the board size is read, then it is 10×10.

nodes.title: On each move the agent chooses one of 3 moves relative to its heading: straight, turn left, turn right.

criteria: Given a snake heading right, when it turns left, then its head moves up one cell and its heading becomes up.
Given any heading, when any of the 3 moves is chosen, then the snake never reverses into its own neck.

nodes.title: Eating food makes the snake 1 cell longer, gives a reward of +1, and places a new food on an empty cell.

criteria: Given food directly ahead, when the snake moves straight, then its length goes up by 1, the move's plain reward is +1, and one new food appears on a cell not covered by the snake.

nodes.title: Moving into a wall or into the snake's own body ends the game with a reward of −1.

criteria: Given the head next to a wall, when the snake moves into the wall, then the game ends and the move's reward is −1.
Given the head next to a body cell that will still be occupied after the move, when the snake moves into it, then the game ends and the move's reward is −1.

nodes.title: Every move that neither eats nor kills has a plain reward of 0.

criteria: Given a move into an empty cell, when it is made, then its plain reward is 0.

nodes.title: At every move the agent sees exactly 11 yes/no facts: danger straight, danger left, danger right; heading up, down, left, right; food is up, down, left, right of the head.

criteria: Given the head next to the top wall while heading up, when the facts are read, then "danger straight" is yes and "heading up" is yes.
Given food above and to the left of the head, when the facts are read, then "food is up" and "food is left" are yes and "food is down" and "food is right" are no.
Given a cell occupied by the body or a wall next to the head on its left, when the facts are read, then "danger left" is yes.

nodes.title: A game ends after 100 moves in a row without eating.

criteria: Given a snake that has gone 100 moves since its last food (or since the start), when the 100th move is made without eating, then the game ends and that move's plain reward is 0.

nodes.title: The same game seed and the same moves always give the same game.

criteria: Given a game seed and a list of moves, when the game is played twice, then every board, food position, reward and ending is identical.

nodes.title: The random player picks each move uniformly at random from the 3 moves.

criteria: Given 30,000 random-player moves, when the share of each move is counted, then each is between 32% and 35%.

nodes.title: The scripted bot moves toward the food, never making a move that kills it immediately when a safe move exists.

criteria: Given food to the left and the left cell free, when the bot moves, then it turns left.
Given food straight ahead and a wall straight ahead with the right cell free, when the bot moves, then it turns right.
Given several safe moves equally close to the food, when the bot moves, then it prefers straight, then left, then right.

nodes.title: When every move kills it, the scripted bot goes straight.

criteria: Given danger straight, left and right, when the bot moves, then it goes straight and the game ends.

nodes.title: The tank's random swimmer picks each move with a uniformly random direction and a speed drawn uniformly from 0 to 2.5 units per second.

criteria: Given 10,000 random-swimmer moves, when their directions are sorted into four equal quarters of the circle, then each quarter holds between 23% and 27% of them.
Given 10,000 random-swimmer moves, when their speeds are averaged, then the mean is between 1.2 and 1.3.

nodes.title: When the tank's scripted bot sees the ball, it swims at 2.5 units per second directly away from the ball.

criteria: Given the ball seen at relative position (1, 0), when the bot moves, then its swim velocity is (−2.5, 0).

nodes.title: When the tank's scripted bot doesn't see the ball, it stays still.

criteria: Given the ball seen as no, when the bot moves, then its swim velocity is (0, 0).

nodes.title: In each comparison, the tank baselines play with the same fish count and view radius as the learner they are compared with.

criteria: Given a 5-fish, wide-view learner, when its baselines are scored, then they play the same test tanks with 5 fish and the wide view.

nodes.title: The table learner updates the score of the move it just made from the reward plus the discounted best score of the situation it reached (a one-step Q-learning update), after every move.

criteria: Given a known table, situation, move, reward and next situation, when one update is applied, then the new score equals the hand-computed Q-learning update for the run's learning rate and discount.
Given a move that ended the game, when the update is applied, then the next situation contributes nothing.

nodes.title: While training, the table learner sometimes picks a random move instead of its best one, at a rate that falls over the run from a starting rate to a floor saved with the run's settings.

criteria: Given a run's exploration settings, when the rate is read at the start, the middle and the end of training, then it matches the saved schedule at each point.

nodes.title: During test games the table learner always picks its highest-scored move.

criteria: Given a trained table, when a test game is played twice from the same seed, then both games are identical.

nodes.title: The learning update is written in the project; no ready-made learning algorithm is used.

criteria: Given the trained table learner, when its learning steps are traced, then each one is code written in the project.

nodes.title: The plain rung learns from each move right after it is made, using that move's reward plus the discounted best score of the next situation as its target.

criteria: Given a known function, move, reward and next situation, when one update is applied, then the target equals the hand-computed value and the function's score for that move moves toward it.

nodes.title: The replay-buffer rung stores past moves and learns from batches drawn at random from that store.

criteria: Given a store of past moves and a seed, when a batch is drawn, then every move in it comes from the store and the same seed draws the same batch.
Given a store at its saved capacity, when a new move is added, then the oldest move is dropped.

nodes.title: The target-network rung computes its targets from a frozen copy of the learner, refreshed every fixed number of updates saved with the run's settings.

criteria: Given the refresh interval, when updates run between two refreshes, then the copy does not change; when the interval is reached, the copy equals the learner.

nodes.title: The Double DQN rung chooses the next situation's best move with the learner, and scores that move with the frozen copy.

criteria: Given a learner and a copy that disagree on the next situation's best move, when the target is computed, then it uses the copy's score for the learner's chosen move.

nodes.title: Each rung differs from the rung before only by the piece it adds; every other setting is the same.

criteria: Given the saved settings of two neighbouring rungs, when they are compared, then the only differences are the added piece and its own settings.

nodes.title: While training, each rung explores with the same falling random-move rate as TAB-02; during test games it always picks its highest-scored move.

criteria: Given a trained rung, when a test game is played twice from the same seed, then both games are identical.

nodes.title: The learning updates of every rung are written in the project; no ready-made learning algorithm is used.

criteria: Given any trained rung, when its learning steps are traced, then each one is code written in the project.

nodes.title: The shaped reward is the plain reward plus 0.1 for a move that brings the head closer to the food and minus 0.1 for a move that takes it further away, measured in grid steps to the food that was on the board before the move.

criteria: Given a move that cuts the distance to the food from 5 to 4, when it is made, then the shaped reward is +0.1.
Given a move that raises the distance from 4 to 5, when it is made, then the shaped reward is −0.1.
Given a move that eats the food, when it is made, then the shaped reward is +1.1.

nodes.title: A move that ends the game by collision has a shaped reward of −1, with no nudge.

criteria: Given a move into a wall, when it is made, then the shaped reward is −1.

nodes.title: Every Snake run uses either the plain or the shaped reward for training, and saves which.

criteria: Given a finished Snake run, when its saved settings are read, then they name its reward.

nodes.title: Test scores never use the shaped reward; they always count food eaten.

criteria: Given the same agent tested once after plain training and once after shaped training, when the scores are read, then both are food eaten per game.

nodes.title: The plain-versus-shaped comparison trains the Double DQN rung on each reward, with every other setting the same.

criteria: Given the plain and shaped runs of that comparison, when their saved settings are compared, then the only difference is the reward.

nodes.title: A training run trains one learner from one training seed on one environment setup: Snake with one reward (the table learner or one DQN rung), or the tank with one fish count and one view radius (one policy-gradient rung).

criteria: Given a learner, an environment setup and a seed, when a run is started with one action, then it trains that learner on that setup with that seed and nothing else.

nodes.title: Each run saves its settings, seed, learning curve, final agent and test games.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its saved evidence is opened, then all five are there.

nodes.title: Rerunning from a run's saved settings and seed gives the same result.

criteria: Given a finished run, when it is run again on the same laptop from its saved settings and seed, then the test score at every curve point is identical.

nodes.title: While a run trains, it shows the steps trained so far, the latest test score and the time elapsed.

criteria: Given a run in progress, when a curve point is reached, then the display updates all three.

nodes.title: A run never overwrites another run's evidence.

criteria: Given two runs with the same learner, reward and seed, when both finish, then both sets of evidence are kept.

nodes.title: A run that stops before it finishes is marked incomplete and is left out of every comparison.

criteria: Given a run stopped by hand partway through, when comparisons are made, then it is listed as incomplete and its numbers are not used.

nodes.title: A run still training at 60 minutes stops, saves what it has, and is marked over the time limit.

criteria: Given a run that reaches 60 minutes, when the limit passes, then training stops, its evidence so far is saved, it is marked over the time limit, and it is left out of every comparison.

nodes.title: Training, testing, saving evidence and replay work for a second environment without changes to them.

criteria: Given a minimal second environment used only for this check, when it is trained, tested and replayed, then none of the training, testing, saving or replay behavior had to change.

nodes.title: After the fish tank is added, Snake runs saved before it still reproduce, compare and replay identically.

criteria: Given a Snake run saved before the tank was added, when it is rerun on the same laptop from its saved settings and seed, then the test score at every curve point is identical to the saved one.
Given the Snake comparisons and replays made before the tank was added, when they are made again, then every result and every replayed game is identical.

nodes.title: Every agent is scored on the same 100 test games of its environment setup, each started from a fixed test seed that is never used in training.

criteria: Given any two agents on the same environment setup, when they are tested, then they play games from the same 100 test seeds.
Given any training run, when its game seeds are compared with the test seeds, then none match.

nodes.title: An agent's test score is the mean of its game scores over the 100 test games: food eaten per game in Snake, and the game score of TANK-10 (mean seconds survived per fish) in the tank.

criteria: Given 100 Snake test games with known food eaten, when the score is computed, then it equals their mean.
Given 100 tank test games with known game scores, when the score is computed, then it equals their mean.

nodes.title: Each run's learning curve is its test score against steps trained, at 20 evenly spaced points, with the random player's and the scripted bot's scores drawn as lines on the same chart; the chart follows the dataviz skill.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its curve is opened, then it shows 20 test scores in order of steps trained, plus both baseline lines.
Given the 5 seeds of one learner, when their combined curve is opened, then it shows the mean across seeds at each point with the spread across seeds.

nodes.title: Each learner's final agent is compared with each baseline using the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given the 100 test-game scores of each of the learner's 5 seed runs, and the baseline's scores on the same 100 games. The learner beats the baseline when its score is higher and the difference is significant at 5% after correcting for the number of comparisons in the report; it ties when the difference is not significant; otherwise it loses.

criteria: Given 5 complete seed runs of a learner, when the comparison is made, then the report states beats, ties or loses against each baseline, with the test's result.
Given fewer than 5 complete seed runs, when the comparison is requested, then it is not made, and the report lists the missing seeds.

nodes.title: Each added piece gets a before-and-after comparison with the rung below it, made the same way as EVAL-04. In Snake: table learner → plain DQN, plain → + replay buffer, + replay buffer → + target network, + target network → + Double DQN, and plain reward → shaped reward. In the tank: REINFORCE → + learned baseline, + learned baseline → actor-critic, actor-critic → PPO (all with 1 fish and the short view), 1-fish PPO → 5-fish PPO (short view), and 5-fish PPO short view → wide view. Every outcome counts: better, worse, or no difference.

criteria: Given 5 complete seed runs of both rungs, when the comparison is made, then the report states better, worse or no difference, with the test's result and both rungs' combined curves on one chart.

nodes.title: Every comparison result holds a written explanation; a result with no explanation is shown as unexplained.

criteria: Given a comparison result with an empty explanation, when the report is opened, then that result is marked unexplained.
Given a tie or a no-difference result with an explanation, when the report is opened, then it is marked explained.

nodes.title: Each environment is done when its top learner beats the random player, beats or ties the scripted bot, every comparison in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05 for that environment has a result, and every tie and no-difference result is explained. Snake's top learner is the Double DQN agent; the tank's is 5-fish, short-view PPO.

criteria: Given a Double DQN agent that beats both baselines and all comparisons made and explained, when the done check runs, then it reports done.
Given a Double DQN agent that ties the scripted bot with the tie explained, when the done check runs, then it reports done.
Given a tie with the scripted bot left unexplained, when the done check runs, then it reports not done and names the missing explanation.
Given a Double DQN agent that ties or loses to the random player, when the done check runs, then it reports not done.

Given 5-fish, short-view PPO that beats the random swimmer, ties the scripted bot with the tie explained, and every tank comparison made and explained, when the done check runs, then it reports the tank done.
Given 5-fish, wide-view PPO that beats the scripted bot while 5-fish, short-view PPO loses to it, when the done check runs, then it reports the tank not done.

nodes.title: Any saved test game of any saved agent, the baselines included, can be watched as a replay.

criteria: Given a finished run, when one of its test games is chosen, then the replay plays it from the first move to the end.

nodes.title: A Snake replay shows the board, the snake, the food, the move number, the food eaten so far, and how the game ended.

criteria: Given a replay at any move, when it is shown, then all of these are visible; at the end, the ending (wall, body, 100 moves without food, full board) is shown.

nodes.title: At every move of a Snake learner's game, the replay shows the agent's score for each of the 3 moves, with the chosen move marked.

criteria: Given a table learner or DQN replay at any move, when it is shown, then 3 scores are visible and the chosen one is marked.
Given a baseline replay, when it is shown, then the move scores are shown as not applicable.

nodes.title: The replay can be paused, resumed, and stepped forward one step at a time.

criteria: Given a paused replay, when "step" is chosen, then it advances exactly one step and stays paused.

nodes.title: The replay speed can be set from 1 to 30 steps per second.

criteria: Given a speed of 5 steps per second, when it plays for 10 seconds, then it advances 50 steps (±2).

nodes.title: A replay of a saved test game is identical to the game that was scored.

criteria: Given a saved test game, when it is replayed, then every state, move and score matches the saved game.

nodes.title: A saved agent can play and be watched on a fresh game from any seed chosen at the time.

criteria: Given a saved agent and a new seed, when the game is watched twice, then both games are identical.

nodes.title: A tank replay shows the tank, the ball, every fish still swimming, the time in seconds, the number of fish still swimming, and the time each removed fish was removed.

criteria: Given a tank replay at any step, when it is shown, then all of these are visible; at the end, the ending (every fish removed, or the 60-second cap) is shown.

nodes.title: At every step of a tank learner's game, each fish still swimming shows an arrow for its chosen swim velocity and a number for how sure it was: the spread of its move choice, smaller meaning surer.

criteria: Given a policy-gradient replay at any step, when it is shown, then every fish still swimming has an arrow and a spread number.
Given a tank baseline replay, when it is shown, then the arrows and spreads are shown as not applicable.

nodes.title: The tank is a circle of radius 10 holding one ball and a fixed number of fish, 1 or 5, saved with the run.

criteria: Given any tank game, when it starts, then the tank's radius is 10, it holds exactly one ball, and the number of fish is the run's 1 or 5.

nodes.title: The ball, of radius 0.5, moves at a constant 2 units per second and bounces off the tank wall like a mirror.

criteria: Given the ball reaching the wall, when it bounces, then it leaves at the same angle to the wall's normal as it arrived, on the other side of the normal.
Given any step of any game, when the ball's speed is measured, then it is 2 units per second.

nodes.title: Each game starts with the ball at the centre heading in a direction set by the game seed, and each fish at a seed-chosen spot between 5 units from the centre and the wall.

criteria: Given any game, when it starts, then the ball is at the centre and every fish is between 5 and 9.75 units from the centre.
Given the same game seed twice, when both games start, then the ball's direction and every fish's spot are identical.

nodes.title: Every 0.1 seconds of tank time, each fish still swimming chooses a move: a swim velocity (x, y) in tank directions, capped at a speed of 2.5 units per second.

criteria: Given a fish that chooses velocity (1, 0), when the step runs, then it moves 0.1 units in the x direction.
Given a fish that chooses velocity (3, 4), when the step runs, then it swims at 2.5 units per second in direction (0.6, 0.8) and moves 0.25 units.

nodes.title: A fish, of radius 0.25, can't leave the tank: a move that would carry it past the wall stops it at the wall.

criteria: Given a fish touching the wall that swims straight outward, when the step runs, then it stays inside the tank, touching the wall.

nodes.title: Fish swim through each other unharmed.

criteria: Given two fish whose paths cross, when the step runs, then both finish their moves and both are still swimming.

nodes.title: At the end of each step, the ball removes every fish whose edge touches it (centres within 0.75 units); a removed fish takes no more moves and is no longer seen by other fish.

criteria: Given a fish whose centre ends a step 0.7 units from the ball's centre, when the step ends, then the fish is removed.
Given a fish whose centre ends a step 0.8 units from the ball's centre, when the step ends, then the fish is still swimming.
Given a removed fish, when the other fish's views are read, then none of them sees it.

nodes.title: A tank game ends when every fish is removed, or at 60 seconds of tank time (600 steps); until then it goes on for the fish still swimming.

criteria: Given 5 fish of which 4 are removed, when the steps continue, then the game goes on until the last fish is removed or 600 steps have run.
Given a fish still swimming after 600 steps, when the 600th step ends, then the game ends.

nodes.title: A fish's reward is +0.1 for each step it survives, and 0 for the step in which it is removed, which ends its experience; there is no other reward.

criteria: Given a fish that survives a step, when the step ends, then its reward is +0.1.
Given a fish removed during a step, when the step ends, then its reward is 0 and it has no further steps.
Given a fish that survives all 600 steps, when its rewards are summed, then the total is 60.

nodes.title: A fish's score is the seconds of tank time it survived, from 0 to 60, and a game's score is the mean over all its fish, removed ones included.

criteria: Given 5 fish that survive 10, 20, 30, 60 and 60 seconds, when the game is scored, then its score is 36.
Given 1 fish removed at 12.5 seconds, when the game is scored, then its score is 12.5.

nodes.title: At every step, each fish sees exactly 11 numbers about what lies within its view radius: for the ball, whether it is seen, its position relative to the fish (2 numbers) and its velocity relative to the fish (2); for the wall, whether it is seen and the offset from the fish to the wall's nearest point (2); for the nearest other fish, whether it is seen and its position relative to the fish (2). Anything beyond the radius is seen as no, and its numbers are 0.

criteria: Given the short view and the ball 3 units away, when the fish's view is read, then the ball is seen as yes and its relative position and velocity are the true ones.
Given the short view and the ball 5 units away, when the view is read, then the ball is seen as no and its 4 numbers are 0.
Given the short view and a fish at the centre of the tank, when the view is read, then the wall is seen as no and its 2 numbers are 0.
Given a 1-fish game, when the view is read, then the nearest other fish is seen as no and its 2 numbers are 0.

nodes.title: A fish's view radius is either 4 units (the short view) or 20 units (the wide view, which spans the whole tank), saved with the run.

criteria: Given the wide view, when any fish's view is read at any step, then the ball and the wall are seen as yes, and so is the nearest other fish if one is still swimming.

nodes.title: The same game seed and the same moves always give the same game.

criteria: Given a game seed and a list of moves for every fish, when the game is played twice, then every position, removal, reward and ending is identical.

nodes.title: The REINFORCE rung, after each game, raises the chance of each move a fish made in proportion to the discounted return that followed it.

criteria: Given a known policy, a finished game, the run's learning rate and discount, when one update is applied, then the change to the policy equals the hand-computed REINFORCE step.

nodes.title: The learned-baseline rung weights each move by its return minus a learned estimate of the return from the situation it was made in, and trains that estimate toward the returns seen.

criteria: Given a move with return 4.0 from a situation estimated at 3.0, when its weight is computed, then the weight is 1.0.
Given a situation whose estimate is below the returns seen from it, when the estimate is trained, then the estimate rises toward them.

nodes.title: The actor-critic rung weights each move by its reward plus the discounted estimate of the next situation, minus the estimate of the situation it was made in, and learns after every fixed number of steps saved with the run's settings.

criteria: Given a known reward, discount and two estimates, when a move's weight is computed, then it equals the hand-computed value.
Given the run's steps per update, when training runs, then an update happens after every that many steps, not only at the end of a game.

nodes.title: The PPO rung learns from each batch of experience in a fixed number of passes, and caps each move's change in chance at a clip range, both saved with the run's settings.

criteria: Given a move whose chance has already risen past 1 + the clip range times its chance when collected, and a positive weight, when the update is computed, then that move pushes the policy no further.
Given the run's passes per batch, when one batch is learned from, then the number of passes equals it.

nodes.title: Each tank setup differs from the one it is compared with only by the piece it adds: one rung from the rung below, 5-fish PPO from 1-fish PPO only by the fish count, and wide-view PPO from short-view PPO only by the view radius.

criteria: Given the saved settings of any two setups compared in EVAL-05, when they are compared, then the only differences are the added piece and its own settings.

nodes.title: With several fish, every fish uses the same policy on its own view, and every fish's experience trains it.

criteria: Given a 5-fish run, when moves are chosen, then every fish's move comes from the one policy applied to that fish's own 11 numbers.
Given a 5-fish run, when an update is applied, then it learns from the experience of all 5 fish up to each one's removal.

nodes.title: While training, each fish picks its move at random from the policy's spread; during test games it takes the policy's most likely move.

criteria: Given a trained policy, when a test game is played twice from the same seed, then both games are identical.

nodes.title: The learning updates of every rung are written in the project; no ready-made learning algorithm is used.

criteria: Given any trained rung, when its learning steps are traced, then each one is code written in the project.

nodes.title: All training and test experience comes from the agents playing in the lab's environments, Snake and the fish tank; no outside data is used.

criteria: Given any run, when its inputs are listed, then the only source of games is the run's own environment, started from the run's own seeds.

nodes.title: Each training run in either environment, including its test games, finishes in under 1 hour (60 minutes) on the laptop's processor.

criteria: Checked by the elapsed time saved with each run; RUN-07 stops any run that reaches 60 minutes.

nodes.title: Training, testing and replay run on the Apple Silicon laptop with no NVIDIA graphics card.

criteria: Checked by running every learner's training, a comparison and a replay on that laptop.
